title: Document attachments with size, count and type limits
description:
Approvers keep asking owners to email the receipt or the signed contract next to a document, and those copies are not tied to the review. This lets the owner attach files to a draft, stored with the document and readable by everyone who can read the document.

- Migration V3 adds `document_attachment` (file name, content type, size, SHA-256, `bytea` content, uploader, time) with an index on `(document_id, id)`.
- `POST /api/v1/documents/{id}/attachments` takes `multipart/form-data` with one part named `file` and answers 201 with `Location` and the stored metadata. Only the owner may attach, and only while the document is a draft (`DocumentStateMachine.requireAttachable`: 403 for another user who can see it, 409 `invalid-transition` once submitted, also after a rejection or a withdrawal). Outsiders get 404, as on every document route.
- Limits come from the new `workflow.attachments.*` settings (`AttachmentSettings`, validated at startup): `max-bytes` per file (5 MiB by default, 413 with the new `too-large` problem), `max-per-document` (10, then 409 `conflict`) and `allowed-types` (PDF, PNG, JPEG, plain text; the part's content type is compared without parameters and case, anything else is 415). An empty file or a name with control characters is a 400; a name sent with a client-side path keeps only its last segment.
- The upload runs under the document row lock (`lockVisible`), like every other change to a document, so two uploads at the limit cannot both pass the count check and an upload cannot slip in after a concurrent submit.
- The servlet container's multipart limits are derived from `max-bytes` (a `MultipartConfigElement` bean replaces Boot's `spring.servlet.multipart` limits), so Tomcat stops reading an oversized file at the limit; that `MaxUploadSizeExceededException`, an unreadable multipart body and a missing `file` part are mapped to problem details instead of framework bodies. A request that is not multipart gets the existing 415 problem, now saying multipart is expected. The container's request-size limit is `max-bytes` + 64 KiB (room for the part headers and boundaries): a request more than 64 KiB over the file limit is refused from its declared size with 413 and `Connection: close` before its body is read, so a client that keeps writing the body may see the connection closed before it reads the 413 (curl reads it; `java.net.http` reports an `IOException`). `max-swallow-size` is left at its default. `application.yml` raises `server.tomcat.max-part-header-size` from Tomcat's 512 bytes to 4KB, so the part headers of a 200-character file name in a non-Latin script (up to 800 bytes of UTF-8 in the name alone) are accepted rather than refused as too large.
- `GET .../attachments` lists the files without their content (a constructor projection, so the `bytea` column is not read); `GET .../attachments/{attachmentId}` downloads one with its stored type, `Content-Disposition: attachment` (RFC 5987 file name) and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Both use `DocumentAccess.visible`, and an attachment is looked up together with the document id in the path. `DELETE .../attachments/{attachmentId}` removes a file under the same owner/draft rule.
- Audit rows `ATTACHMENT_ADDED` (id, size, type) and `ATTACHMENT_REMOVED`; file names and contents are not logged or audited.

Tests: `AttachmentApiTest` (upload and download by an approver after submit with the stored SHA-256, strangers 404 and viewers read-only, size/type/count limits, locked after submit) and a real-HTTP case in `RealHttpTest` (a file exactly at the limit round-trips, one byte more is stopped by the container with a 413 problem, a missing part is 400, JSON is 415; a 200-character CJK file name is stored, and a request declaring 6 MiB, read by a client that stops writing after the part headers, gets 413 with `Connection: close`). `AttachmentApiTest` also checks that a file name is counted in characters (code points), not UTF-16 units: 200 supplementary-plane characters are accepted and 201 refused. `IntegrationTestBase` uses small limits and truncates the new table. README: concepts, settings, routes and the new problem slug.
